summary: Tower at Tilden Lake (Ellsmere Village), Ontario, on a hobby still-standing list; the village was a 1920s-30s timber-mill site; a visitor says its ladder's bottom is removed.

visit.trail_note: Visitor note on Firelookout.ca: walked across a bridge, then hiked to the tower; the bottom of the ladder has been removed.

evidence.supports: Listed on the still-standing list as Lyman Tower at Tilden Lake, Ont.
Tilden Lake was a timber mill in the 1920s and 1930s
evidence.quote: Tilden Lake was a timber mill in the 1920s and '30s and part of the '40s.

evidence.supports: Tilden Lake is an unincorporated community
The mill was owned by the Ellsmere brothers
evidence.quote: The mill was owned by the Ellsmere Brothers and employed over 500 strong lumberjacks and millers.

evidence.supports: A fire destroyed the mill; it shut down for good in the early 1950s for economic reasons
evidence.quote: A fire destroyed the mill and it shut down for good in the early 1950s for economic reasons.

evidence.supports: Main village road named for the brothers
evidence.quote: The main village road was named for the brothers and now is called the village road and Ellsmere road.

evidence.supports: Visitor describes the tower as a relic of the era of manpower fire watch
evidence.quote: Near the village of Ellesmere is a relic of a time when manpower was the best way to watch for the signs of a forest fire.

evidence.supports: View from the base is unremarkable; forest on all sides
evidence.quote: The view from the base of the tower is unremarkable as the forest surrounds it on all sides.

evidence.supports: Visitor walked across a bridge and hiked to the tower
evidence.quote: we walked across it and then enjoyed our hike to the tower

evidence.supports: Bottom of the ladder removed; visitor warns against climbing the unmaintained structure
evidence.quote: the bottom of the ladder has been removed so that you DON"T climb the unmaintained structure

evidence.supports: MNR no longer maintains the listed towers; visitors asked not to climb
evidence.quote: The MNR no longer maintains them so please refrain from climbing.

evidence.supports: MNR decided as of 2013 to remove many still-standing towers
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these still standing towers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The list gives Tilden Lake; Firelookout.ca gives Ellsmere Village. Wikipedia describes Tilden Lake as a mill settlement whose main village road was named for the Ellsmere brothers, so the two names probably refer to the same community.

notes_for_editor: Brief has no local_unit; no source gives a district. Location is resolved by treating Tilden Lake and Ellsmere Village as one community, an inference from the Wikipedia article, which is a single-source page tagged for citations. The visitor note is undated and the walk is one visitor's account. No build date, height, design, staffing or access level found, so none are given; access is omitted because no source says whether the public may visit. Follow-up: Forest History Ontario archives, MNR records, and local Temagami or North Bay history.
